# 1 Kings Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 173r–174r | **Source Image:** 1KI_001_page_001.jpg, 1KI_001_page_002.jpg, 1KI_001_page_003.jpg

---

**1** King David was now very old. No matter how many blankets they piled on him, he could not stay warm.

**2** His servants said, "Let us find a young virgin to attend the king. She can lie beside you and keep you warm, my lord."

**3** So they searched throughout Israel for a beautiful young woman and found Abishag from Shunem. They brought her to the king.

**4** She was stunningly beautiful. She became the king's attendant and cared for him, but the king was not intimate with her.

**5** Meanwhile, Adonijah son of Haggith began promoting himself, declaring, "I will be king!" He acquired chariots, horses, and fifty men to run ahead of him.

**6** His father had never once challenged him by asking, "What do you think you're doing?" Adonijah was also very handsome, and he was born next after Absalom.

**7** He conspired with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they threw their support behind him.

**8** But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's elite warriors did not side with Adonijah.

**9** Adonijah held a great sacrificial feast — sheep, cattle, and fattened calves — at the Stone of Zoheleth near En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's other sons, and all the royal officials of Judah.

**10** But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the elite warriors, or his brother Solomon.

**11** Nathan went to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and asked, "Haven't you heard? Adonijah son of Haggith has made himself king — and David doesn't even know!

**12** Let me advise you how to save your life and the life of your son Solomon.

**13** Go immediately to King David and say, 'My lord the king, didn't you swear to me that my son Solomon would succeed you and sit on your throne? Why then has Adonijah become king?'

**14** While you're still talking with the king, I'll come in and back up everything you've said."

**15** So Bathsheba went to the king in his private chamber. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was attending him.

**16** Bathsheba bowed low before the king. He asked, "What is it?"

**17** She answered, "My lord, you swore to me by the LORD your God, 'Your son Solomon will reign after me and sit on my throne.'

**18** But now Adonijah has become king — and you, my lord, don't even know about it!

**19** He has sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the king's sons, plus Abiathar the priest and Joab the army commander. But he has not invited your servant Solomon.

**20** My lord the king, all Israel is watching you, waiting for you to announce who will succeed you on the throne.

**21** If you don't act, the moment you die, Solomon and I will be treated as criminals."

**22** While she was still speaking, Nathan the prophet arrived.

**23** They announced to the king, "Nathan the prophet is here." Nathan came before the king and bowed facedown.

**24** Nathan said, "My lord the king, did you declare that Adonijah would succeed you and sit on your throne?

**25** Because today he went down and sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep. He invited all the king's sons, the army commanders, and Abiathar the priest. Right now they are eating and drinking with him, shouting, 'Long live King Adonijah!'

**26** But he did not invite me — your servant — or Zadok the priest, or Benaiah son of Jehoiada, or your servant Solomon.

**27** Has my lord the king authorized this without telling your servants who should sit on the throne after you?"

**28** King David responded, "Bring Bathsheba to me." She came and stood before the king.

**29** The king swore an oath: "As surely as the LORD lives — the God who has rescued me from every danger —

**30** I will carry out today what I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel: Solomon your son will reign after me and sit on my throne in my place."

**31** Bathsheba bowed facedown and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"

**32** King David said, "Summon Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." When they arrived,

**33** the king told them, "Take my personal guard, put my son Solomon on my own royal mule, and escort him down to Gihon.

**34** There, Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel. Sound the trumpet and shout, 'Long live King Solomon!'

**35** Then escort him back up, and he will take his seat on my throne. He will reign in my place, for I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah."

**36** Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, confirm it!

**37** As the LORD has been with my lord the king, may he be with Solomon — and make his throne even greater than yours!"

**38** So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethite and Pelethite guards went down. They put Solomon on King David's mule and brought him to Gihon.

**39** There Zadok the priest took the horn of sacred oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. They blew the trumpet, and all the people shouted, "Long live King Solomon!"

**40** The whole crowd followed him back up, playing flutes and celebrating with such tremendous joy that the ground shook with the noise.

**41** Adonijah and all his guests heard the commotion just as they were finishing their feast. When Joab heard the trumpet, he demanded, "What's all that noise from the city?"

**42** While Joab was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. "Come in," Adonijah said. "A man like you must be bringing good news."

**43** "Not at all," Jonathan answered. "Our lord King David has made Solomon king!

**44** The king sent Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the royal guard with him. They put him on the king's own mule.

**45** Zadok and Nathan anointed him king at Gihon, and they've come back up celebrating. The whole city is in an uproar — that's the noise you've been hearing.

**46** What's more, Solomon is already sitting on the royal throne.

**47** The king's officials have even come to congratulate King David, saying, 'May God make Solomon's name even more famous than yours and his throne even greater!' The king bowed in worship from his bed.

**48** David himself said, 'Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, who has let me see with my own eyes a successor on my throne today.'"

**49** At this, all of Adonijah's guests panicked. They got up and scattered, each going his own way.

**50** Adonijah himself was terrified of Solomon. He rushed to the altar and grabbed hold of its horns.

**51** Solomon was told, "Adonijah is afraid of you and is clinging to the horns of the altar. He says, 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he won't execute his servant.'"

**52** Solomon replied, "If he proves to be loyal, not a hair on his head will be touched. But if he is found to be disloyal, he will die."

**53** King Solomon sent men to bring Adonijah down from the altar. Adonijah came and bowed before King Solomon. Solomon told him, "Go home."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **1:1-4 — David's decline**: The opening is deliberately anticlimactic. The great warrior-king who conquered Jerusalem and defeated nations cannot keep warm. The political crisis that follows grows directly from this physical weakness — David's inability to act creates the vacuum Adonijah exploits.

2. **1:5-6 — "his father had never challenged him"**: This devastating parenthetical explains everything. David's parenting failures — already visible with Amnon and Absalom — continue with Adonijah. The same permissiveness that enabled Absalom's rebellion enables this one.

3. **1:33 — "my own royal mule"**: In the ancient Near East, riding the king's personal mount was a public declaration of succession. This wasn't a private ceremony — it was political theater designed to be seen by the entire city.

4. **1:40 — "the ground shook"**: The Hebrew says the earth "was split" (tippaqeah) — a hyperbolic expression for deafening noise, but also an echo of theophanic language. Solomon's coronation is presented as a divinely endorsed event.

5. **1:50 — the altar horns**: Adonijah's flight to the altar transforms a political crisis into a theological one. By grasping the altar's horns, he claims divine sanctuary — forcing Solomon to make his first ruling as king a question of mercy versus justice.

— PNEUMA
